title: Competitive Landscape Map
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: A clickable spectrum of the five kinds of alternative to Jordan's mobile dog-grooming idea, ordered by how directly each solves the same problem: do-nothing alternative, current workaround, substitute solution, indirect competitor, and direct competitor. Each step along the line adds one thing (a fix, a dedicated offer, the same problem, the same approach). Selecting a node shows its definition, Jordan's example, why it sits there, and where it falls short. The spectrum turns vertical on narrow screens.

prerequisites: Chapter 7 reading through Direct, Indirect, and Substitute Competitors
educational.topic: Alternatives and the competitive landscape: ordering a venture's alternatives by how directly each solves the same problem
learningObjectives: Differentiate existing alternatives to a venture as the do-nothing alternative, a current workaround, an indirect competitor or substitute, or a direct competitor, by their directness in solving the same problem
Name the single difference that separates two neighboring alternatives on the spectrum
Identify where each alternative falls short for the target customer as raw material for a market gap

controls.label: ← Less direct
controls.purpose: Select the neighboring node one step toward the do-nothing end (also the left arrow key); with nothing selected, starts at the direct competitor

controls.label: More direct →
controls.purpose: Select the neighboring node one step toward the direct-competitor end (also the right arrow key); with nothing selected, starts at the do-nothing alternative

controls.label: Clear
controls.purpose: Deselect the node and return the panel to the opening prompt (also the Escape key)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Exploration of a worked example: a clickable ordered spectrum with a detail panel for comparing neighboring categories
keyQuestions: How directly does this alternative solve the same problem as Jordan's offer?
What single difference separates two neighboring alternatives on the spectrum?
Where does each alternative fall short for Jordan's customer?
commonMisconceptions: Only businesses selling something similar count as competitors
Having no visible competitors means the idea has no competition
A substitute and an indirect competitor are the same thing because both are dedicated businesses
assessmentOpportunities: Place an alternative that is not on the map and name the step it has not taken
Explain why the do-nothing alternative is often the toughest competitor
Map one alternative of each kind for one's own venture and name a shortfall they all share
